name: Electro-swing and moisture-swing DAC
principle: Electro-swing adsorption toggles the CO2 affinity of a redox-active material electrochemically: it captures at 400 ppm while charging and releases when discharged. Moisture-swing sorbents capture CO2 when dry and release it when wetted. Verdox's 2020-21 DOE project tuned quinone redox molecules and electrode channels, reporting a channel pressure drop below 1,000 Pa. IEA rates electrochemical DAC at TRL 6.

source.note: NETL project kickoff slides, Verdox electro-swing adsorption DAC (February 2021)
IEA ETP Clean Energy Technology Guide, dataset of 24 July 2026, latest assessment (IEA 1-11 scale): 'Electrochemical DAC (e-DAC)' 6 (2025)

advantages: Operates at ambient temperature and avoids heat input in principle
limitations: The slides give no energy, capacity or cost figures
